findings.obs_text: In Psa 92:5 and Isa 66:18 the Lord's works and thoughts, and people's works and thoughts known to him, are named together: the thoughts stand with the deeds. In Neh 6:9 the enemies think the hands will drop from the work, in Ecc 9:10 there is no work or thought in Sheol, in Mat 21:28 work is the son's task in the case asked about, and in Eph 3:20 God's power at work goes beyond what we think.
findings.grounds: I know their works and their thoughts

findings.obs_text: In 1Sa 20:3 Saul thinks to keep the matter from Jonathan lest he be grieved: the thought is to spare his son grief.

In Mar 6:49 the disciples think they see a ghost and cry out: the cry follows the mistaken thought. In Deu 15:9 the poor brother may cry to the Lord against the one whose unworthy thought made him grudging.
findings.grounds: they thought it was a ghost, and cried out

findings.obs_text: Life and death are what the thought concerns in 1Sa 20:3 (David's oath on the Lord who lives), 1Sa 27:11 and 2Ki 7:12 (none left alive, taking them alive), and Act 26:8 (God raising the dead thought incredible). In Dan 5:10 the queen wishes the king life as his thoughts alarm him, in Luk 13:4 the dead are compared with all who lived in Jerusalem, in Dan 2:30 Daniel claims no wisdom above all the living, and in Heb 4:12 the living word discerns the thoughts.
findings.grounds: the word of God is living and active

older.finding: a reading of the live words, to be read with them: What is called living.
older.reason: it states how live works in a person; the live collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Deu 15:9 the unworthy thought in the heart is that the year of release is near, so the poor brother is refused: the thought turns the release into a reason to withhold. In Jer 40:4 Jeremiah is released from chains and told to go where he thinks good.
findings.grounds: the year of release is near
